findings.title: V2 canManage() grants global group management to callers with only VIEW permission
findings.body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Any admin with only an all-groups `view` permission therefore passes `groups().requireManage()`.

That check is what guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`. As a result, a view-only admin can:
- create arbitrary top-level groups;
- send an existing group id and move any group in the realm to top level, changing the hierarchy and any role or attribute inheritance that depends on it.

The per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` correctly uses only `MANAGE`. The no-arg variant should do the same.

The interface Javadoc for `canManage()` in `GroupPermissionEvaluator` ("Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") documents the same wrong behavior and should be fixed too. No test checks that an all-groups VIEW permission does not allow creating groups.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body:
In V2, per-group resources are named by the group id (`resolveGroup` returns `group.getId()` and the resource is created with that name). The method instead passes `groupResource.getId()`, the authorization resource UUID, both to `hasPermission` (which calls `findByName`) and to the result set.

Consequences:
1. `findByName(server, resourceId)` never finds the per-group resource, so a per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grant is never recognized here. It silently falls back to the all-groups resource.
2. The all-groups `Groups` resource has type `Groups` (set in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init`), so `findByType` returns it. With an all-groups `view-members`/`manage-members` permission, its resource UUID is added to the set.

The IDs that end up in the set are not group IDs. `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` then put them into the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute, and the user query is restricted to members of a non-existent group, so the search returns nothing. `getUsersCount` computes counts against the same bogus IDs.

In the per-group case the set stays empty, so no DB-level pre-filtering happens. Results are filtered after pagination, and pages can come back empty or incomplete in realms with more than `max` users.

Use `groupResource.getName()` for both the lookup and the collected ID, and skip the type-level `Groups` resource. Add a test with an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission and a user search.

findings.title: NPE / ModelException for realms whose admin-permissions schema predates the Groups type
findings.body:
`AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so nothing migrates existing data. Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this change have no `Groups` type resource and no `manage-membership`, `manage-members` or `view-members` scopes.

For those realms, `getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` returns null. That null is passed unchecked to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`. The result is an NPE, i.e. HTTP 500, on every group endpoint and on user view/manage-by-group checks for any admin without MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS.

Creating a group permission in such a realm also fails: `getOrCreateResource` throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` because the new scopes are missing.

Add a null guard (treat as no permission) and either migrate or lazily create the new type resource and scopes.

findings.title: getResourceName has no handling for the new Groups resource type
findings.body:
`getResourceName` only maps the `Users` type to a human-readable name. For `Groups` it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`.

Per-group resources are created by `getOrCreateResource` with the group id as the name and no display name. Permission representations for groups will therefore show null or a raw UUID instead of the group name, and the all-groups resource will not be shown as "All groups" the way users get "All users".

findings.title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body:
The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementation actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, and the two have different semantics, so the doc is misleading.

In the same file, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` documents `@return Stream of IDs` although it returns a `Set`.
